description: A complete, responsive educational portfolio application that simulates user accounts, virtual balances, transfers, wallets, savings, budgeting, cards, notifications, and administrative management. It must use fictional data and an internal ledger only; it must not connect to real banks or payment networks, process real money, or require KYC.

services.name: Web application
services.description: Responsive customer and administrator interfaces for onboarding, simulated accounts and payments, wallet and recharge simulations, savings, analytics, notifications, cards, profile/settings, and administration.

services.name: Application API
services.description: Authenticated API and business logic for profiles, virtual accounts, atomic simulated ledger operations, payment requests, wallets, beneficiaries, savings, budgets, cards, notifications, and role-protected administration.

questions.question: Which language should the web application use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing and helps maintain a large, feature-rich application.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses standard JavaScript without a compile-time type system.

questions.rationale: No frontend language was specified. TypeScript is recommended for the breadth of the requested UI.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should be used?

options.label: React
options.description: A widely used component-based framework with a broad ecosystem.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A progressive component framework with approachable conventions.

options.label: Angular
options.description: A full-featured framework with integrated application patterns.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: A compiler-based framework for concise component-driven interfaces.

questions.rationale: The specification requires a polished, responsive web UI but does not mandate a framework; React is the recommended default.

questions.question: Are there any additional frontend requirements beyond the requested banking simulator, responsive layouts, accessible forms, theme options, clear transaction states, and customer/admin views?
questions.recommendedChoice: Use the features described in the project specification.
questions.answer: Use the features described in the project specification.

questions.question: Which language should the application API use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Provides typed application logic and strong ecosystem support for API services.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses standard JavaScript for the API without a compile-time type system.

options.label: Python
options.description: Offers a productive language and a mature ecosystem for API development.

options.label: C# (.NET)

questions.question: Which backend framework should be used for the application API?

options.label: NestJS
options.description: A structured TypeScript framework suitable for modular APIs and layered business logic.

options.label: Express
options.description: A minimal Node.js web framework with a large ecosystem.

options.label: FastAPI
options.description: A Python framework with typed request validation and generated API documentation.

options.label: ASP.NET Core
options.description: A mature .NET framework for secure, high-performance APIs.

questions.rationale: No backend framework is mandated. NestJS is recommended for clear modules and server-side authorization and transaction boundaries.

questions.question: Are there any additional backend requirements beyond the requested authentication, role-based authorization, persistent data, atomic simulated ledger operations, validation, duplicate protection, audit history, and API documentation?
questions.recommendedChoice: Use the features described in the project specification.
questions.answer: Use the features described in the project specification.
questions.rationale: The attached specification already defines the API and business logic requirements, including that all financial activity remains simulated.

questions.question: Which data stores should the project use?

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational persistence with transactional guarantees and constraints suited to the simulated ledger.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Managed relational persistence with transactions and constraints for structured application data.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only when the application does not need persistent data.

questions.rationale: The application requires persistent users, accounts, transactions, and audit records, with atomic financial operations; a relational database is required. No file/object storage is specified.

questions.question: Should users sign in to use application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in to access their own simulated accounts and protected application features.

options.label: No
options.description: The application does not require users to sign in.

questions.rationale: The requested application includes registration, login, sessions, personal accounts, and role-protected administrative features. This refers to application sign-in only, not identity-provider or Azure credential selection.
